articles.title_original: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
articles.title_zh: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
facts_zh:
Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
- Published
Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente has resigned - six days after the high-speed train collision in which at least 69 people were killed and dozens injured.

He announced his decision in Congress, after giving evidence on last Wednesday's disaster near the town of Urda, south of the capital Madrid, in which a train smashed into the back of a stationary train.

"A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year," he said - a reference to January's crash on the same line which left 46 people dead.

all_titles.en: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash

articles.title_zh: NTSB says crucial plane parts found three miles from Florida crash site
facts_zh:
NTSB says crucial plane parts found three miles from Florida crash site
- Published
Crucial components of a private jet that crashed in Palm Beach, Florida - including a part that controlled the up-and-down movements of the nose of the plane - were found 1.3 (2 km) to 3.8 miles away from the crash site, an investigator said on Tuesday.
National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigators said they believed parts of the jet may have broken off before the Sunday crash, which killed all nine on board.
The NTSB found "the majority" of the Learjet's left elevator - a control surface on the tail - in three pieces, NTSB board member Tom Chapman said.

Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats

Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.

Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.
The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing.

facts_zh:
Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
- Published
Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others across Ukraine over the last 24 hours.

At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.
He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".

articles.title_original: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
articles.title_zh: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
facts_zh:
Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
- Published
Rio Tinto is ploughing millions of dollars into stopping the poisonous cane toad reaching the Pilbara region of western Australia, where the mining giant has a vast iron ore operation.
The firm, alongside Curtin University in Perth and others, will spend A$28m (£14.5m) building a "toad containment zone" to prevent the pest travelling south.
While the cane toad is not a direct threat to Rio Tinto's business, it produces toxins lethal to native wildlife and poses a threat to Pilbara's ecosystem.

all_titles.en: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia

articles.title_original: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
articles.title_zh: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
facts_zh:
Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
- Published
Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo.
The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings.
It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god.

all_titles.en: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes

facts_zh:
Europe on alert after supermarket freezers hit by cyber-attacks in 10 countries
- Published
A spate of cyber-attacks that hit supermarket chains across at least 10 European countries on Monday has prompted European Union officials to warn of a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply chain.

Supermarkets have reported problems in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Germany and Sweden, and the significant increase in freezer temperatures has forced retailers to discard food.
Temperatures in chains across Europe reportedly rose as high as 50C (122F).

Investigators believe parts of a private jet that crashed in Florida and killed all nine onboard may have broken off while it was in the air.

A tech entrepreneur and his young family, as well as the 20-year-old co-pilot, were among those who died on Sunday.

facts_zh:
Russian bombing kills 31 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
- Published
At least 31 people have been killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Zaporizhia, the Ukrainian regional head has said, describing it as one of the deadliest attacks there since the start of the full-scale invasion.
Mykhailo Semikin said at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in southern Ukraine on Monday and the aid centre collapsed from a "direct hit".
"They had come for help - not to a military facility, not to a frontline position, but to a place where they were supposed to receive support," he wrote on Telegram.

articles.title_zh: US urges Venezuela to release remaining political prisoners

- Published
The US has urged Venezuela to release the remaining political prisoners being held in the South American country.

More than 1,000 political prisoners have been freed since US forces seized Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in a military raid on Caracas on 3 January and took him to New York, where he faces trial on drug-trafficking and torture charges.
But Venezuelan prisoners' rights group Foro Penal says 322 people remain in detention.

Indian tourist killed after two helicopters collide near Everest base camp
- Published
An Indian tourist has died after two helicopters collided while attempting to land near the base camp of Mount Everest, two officials have confirmed to the BBC.

Verified footage of the crash showed the helicopter blades of the two aircraft clipping each other as they came into land at around 08:15 local time (02:30 GMT) in Pheriche, approximately 12km (7 miles) south of Mount Everest Base Camp.
Helicopter company Fishtail Air named the man killed in the crash as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu.

articles.title_original: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
articles.title_zh: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
facts_zh:
Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
- Published
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after the 30-year-old suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.
The forward suffered head and chest injuries during a match against FC Andorra on Monday in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.
De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning, with the Spaniard dying at 07:00 GMT.

all_titles.en: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision

articles.title_original: Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.title_zh: Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
facts_zh:
Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
- Published
The 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been postponed because of a series of deadly attacks on the host country.
The 24-team tournament was scheduled to take place from 7 January to 5 February but has been rescheduled to run from 23 December, 2027 to 21 January, 2028.
In October, a missile attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.

all_titles.en: Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
